mechanism: cyclic rotation of a mode-trivial closed loop + exact identity BS(pi,0)^2 = R(pi) x R(pi)

rule.name: swap_loop_cyclic_fusion_parity
rule.idea: Two consecutive swap-loop gadgets (colocated_mode_swap_loop_pauli_zz) on the same mode pair (m_j, m_k), separated only by qubit-wire gates, share a junction S-S pair once the second gadget is cyclically rotated to start with S. Since the loop L = A*S acts as the identity on both modes (the rectangle closes), L commutes with S, so S*A = S*(A*S)*S^-1 = S*L*S^-1 = L: any cyclic rotation of the 8-gate word implements the same unitary. The basis-change gates between the two gadgets live on qubit wires only and commute with S (which acts on mode wires only), so they pass through unchanged. The adjacent S*S = BS(pi,0)^2 = BS(2pi,0) = exp(-i pi (a^+b+b^+a)); since a^+b+b^+a has eigenvalues n_a+n_b (mod 2) on the relevant subspace, exp(-i pi(a^+b+b^+a)) = R_a(pi) R_b(pi) exactly for any cutoff, for every photon number. Replacing the detected adjacent BS(pi,0), BS(pi,0) pair (with only qubit-only gates in between, which are kept in place) by R(pi) on each of the two mode wires realizes this identity, turning a two-op mode-mode gate pair into two one-op single-mode gates with no change to the overall unitary and no routing impact.

reason: rule never chosen/applied on any benchmark
